answer: A brute force password cracking attack works by systematically trying all possible combinations of passwords for a known user ID until access is granted by the application or system. This method exploits the finite space of possible passwords defined by the password policy in place. Attackers may manually or automatically enter these combinations through the system's interface, often starting with the shortest and simplest passwords, as users typically choose easier passwords if allowed [Source 1][Source 2].
